On some Pixel phones the Wi-Fi chip randomly stops working: Wi-Fi will not turn on or drops by itself, and sometimes Bluetooth goes with it.

What we found: the failure happens in the physical link between the processor and the Wi-Fi chip (PCIe). The driver puts the chip to sleep after just 0.5 s without traffic, and the link has to be re-established every time it wakes up. A faulty link eventually fails at one of those wake-ups, and it gets much worse with heat.

What this app does:
🛡️ Protects actively: it sends a tiny packet to your router every 0.2 s, only over Wi-Fi, so the chip never sits idle, never falls asleep, and never has to wake up again, which is exactly where it fails. It does not modify the chip, the driver or the system, and it needs no root.
📊 Watches and warns: it detects drops, logs temperature and tells you when the phone is cool enough to restart.

If your Wi-Fi is already down:
1. Turn the phone off completely.
2. Let it cool down for 15–20 minutes: no case, no charger, in a cool place or in front of a fan. Never in the freezer or the fridge: condensation can damage it.
3. Turn it on, open Wi-Fi Guardian and turn on Wi-Fi.

This is a workaround for a hardware problem, not a repair. It may use a bit more battery. It is free and open source.
